claims: The Artemis II Orion capsule re-entered Earth's atmosphere on Friday, April 10, 2026.
The Artemis II Orion capsule's entry interface occurred around 7:53 p.m. EDT (4:53 p.m. PDT).
The Artemis II Orion capsule splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California, at 8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT).
The Artemis II Orion capsule's splashdown marked the end of the crewed mission.
The communication blackout lasted approximately 6 minutes starting at 7:53 p.m. EDT.
The Artemis II Orion capsule's drogue chutes deployed at 8:03 p.m. EDT at 22,000 ft.
The Artemis II Orion capsule's main chutes deployed at 8:04 p.m. EDT at 6,000 ft.
The Artemis II Orion capsule traveled at over 24,000 mph during its entry into the atmosphere.
Over 24,000 mph is roughly 35 times the speed of sound.
